dose.note: Applicant popPK of free and adjusted-bound aflibercept from 13 nAMD/DME studies, with an ocular compartment; no comparison stated yet at model build.
dose.srcLabel: FDA Eylea HD clinical pharmacology review 2023
dose.quote: The PopPK analysis included free and adjusted bound aflibercept concentration-time data from 13 clinical studies in patients with nAMD or DME receiving aflibercept as intravenous (IV) or intravitreal (IVT) injections
dose.confidence_note: Model side read from the FDA clinical pharmacology review (Reference ID 5162313, review year 2023; posted in the Drugs@FDA nda/2024 folder). The popPK report date is not given; the BLA followed the pre-BLA meeting of 2022-09-26. Opening entry, proxy-dated to the review year.
dose.judgement: Opens the in-silico track at its first documented use, the 8 mg BLA. The model is the applicant's, built on pooled plasma PK that includes CANDELA, PULSAR and PHOTON; it is a different system from the academic rabbit-half-life decay model (Stewart 2008) and from the rabbit chronic-RNV leak model, so it gets its own model_id.

patient_trials.quote: Aflibercept 8q12 and 8q16 demonstrated non-inferior BCVA gains to aflibercept 2q8

dose.model: Applicant population-PK model of free and bound aflibercept with an ocular compartment (aflibercept 8 mg BLA 761355)
dose.note: PopPK predicted free aflibercept above ocular LLOQ for 15 weeks after 8 mg vs 8.7 weeks after 2 mg; PHOTON 8q12/8q16 non-inferior to 2q8. Built on PHOTON data, so a retrodiction.
dose.short: Post-hoc popPK: 15 vs 8.7 weeks, PHOTON held
dose.srcLabel: FDA Eylea HD clinical pharmacology review 2023
dose.quote: The median time for free aflibercept to reach the adjusted LLOQ in the ocular compartment increased from 8.7 weeks after a 2 mg IVT dose to 15 weeks after an 8 mg IVT dose
dose.confidence_note: The reviewer flagged the ocular prediction as unconfirmed: 'as there is no observed ocular concentration of aflibercept to confirm the prediction, such interpretation should be treated with caution.' Regeneron's 2026 integrated popPK (PMID 42381356, 16 trials, 2744 participants) restates the same system's prediction (14 weeks vs 9-9.5 weeks); same system, no new status.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10, not a prospective dose prediction: the popPK dataset carries PHOTON's own plasma PK (study VGFTe-HD-DME-1934, primary completion 2022-05-30) and the BLA was filed after the 48-week readout, so the 15-week ocular estimate was produced with the q12/q16 answer known. It reproduced the result (12-16-week intervals non-inferior to 2q8 in PHOTON: Brown 2024, registry 2023-11-21), hence retro, within_2x. comparison_stated true: the review itself ties the model's longer ocular exposure to the HD drug effect ('Exploratory analyses suggest the slower ocular clearance and longer duration of free aflibercept ocular exposure of HD aflibercept contribute to the drug effect of HD aflibercept'). Dated 2024 because the only public carrier of the prediction is the review, posted in the nda/2024 folder; the 2023 label does not state the ocular LLOQ times. If the atlas treats FDA reviews as public at approval (2023-08-18), the year is 2023. No tolerability margin is stated by this model (margin_stated false); the ocular NOAEL sits on the toxicology track.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted free-aflibercept ocular exposure 15 weeks (8 mg) vs 8.7 weeks (2 mg) against the 12- and 16-week PHOTON intervals that held

engagement.population: DME and nAMD patients (abicipar/MP0112 aqueous sampling); context Centre-involved DME
engagement.model: Mechanistic translational PK/PD model of abicipar-VEGF binding, rabbit to human (Luu 2020)
engagement.note: Rabbit-built mechanistic model of abicipar-VEGF binding, VEGF expression and turnover, fitted to vitreous, aqueous, choroid, retina and serum PK after 1 mg abicipar.
engagement.quote: The model incorporated abicipar-VEGF binding kinetics, VEGF expression levels, and VEGF turnover rates to describe the ocular and systemic PK data collected from the vitreous, aqueous humor (AH), choroid, retina, and serum of rabbits
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading: the ScienceDirect full text is paywalled (HTTP 403; fc.py scrape returned abstract, introduction and references only). JPET 373(2):184-192, epub 2020-02-25; a correction appeared in JPET 374(3):530. model_filed true: the EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (EMA/CHMP/279665/2020, section 3.2.2) describes 'an in silico mechanistic, multi-compartment PK model' built on ocular tissue data, with human abicipar and VEGF vitreal concentrations simulated over 52 weeks for the 2 mg phase 3 regimens, i.e. this model (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/withdrawal-report/withdrawal-assessment-report-rayoqta_en.pdf).
engagement.judgement: Opens the track at publication; the rabbit data behind it are not separately dated. Separate system from the rabbit chronic-RNV leak model (Rodrigues 2018): that model predicts leak duration in an animal, this one predicts human vitreal free VEGF in silico, so it takes its own model_id rather than a post-hoc refit on the RNV track.

engagement.population: DME and nAMD patients (abicipar/MP0112 aqueous sampling); context Centre-involved DME
engagement.model: Mechanistic translational PK/PD model of abicipar-VEGF binding, rabbit to human (Luu 2020)
engagement.note: Model translated to humans and refitted to DME and nAMD patient serum and aqueous-humor data; it reproduced abicipar-VEGF target engagement already measured in those patients.
engagement.short: Refit to DME aqueous data reproduces VEGF suppression
engagement.quote: The model was translated to humans using human-specific mechanistic parameters and refitted to human serum and AH concentrations from patients with diabetic macular edema and nAMD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled full text). The abstract names no study; the DME patient aqueous data are presumably the MP0112 phase I/II (Campochiaro 2013, PMID 23218689: aqueous MP0112 levels and 'neutralization of VEGF in aqueous humor for 8-12 weeks' after 0.4 mg). The reproduction claim rests on the abstract sentence 'The model quantitatively described abicipar-VEGF target engagement leading to rapid reduction of VEGF and a long duration of VEGF inhibition'. No numeric predicted-vs-observed comparison is given in the abstract, so magnitude is null. model_filed true: the EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (EMA/CHMP/279665/2020, section 3.2.2) describes 'an in silico mechanistic, multi-compartment PK model' built on ocular tissue data, with human abicipar and VEGF vitreal concentrations simulated over 52 weeks for the 2 mg phase 3 regimens, i.e. this model (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/withdrawal-report/withdrawal-assessment-report-rayoqta_en.pdf).
engagement.reason: Refit model reproduces patient VEGF engagement
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10: the human aqueous abicipar and free-VEGF data the model was refitted to were public from 2012 (DME phase I/II) and 2014 (nAMD phase I/II), years before the model (2020), and the abstract reports that the model described that target engagement. Direct readout tier: free VEGF and drug in aqueous humor. comparison_stated true because the paper itself sets the model against the patient data. The DME patients supply the context's patient side; nAMD data were pooled in the same refit. The EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (section 3.2.2, adopted 2020-05-28) states the same comparison in the regulator's words: 'the human model again fitted well against the measured abicipar concentrations in serum and aqueous humor from patients with nAMD and diabetic macular edema, respectively.'

dose.model: Mechanistic translational PK/PD model of abicipar-VEGF binding, rabbit to human (Luu 2020)
dose.note: Model simulated 8-, 12- and 16-week abicipar 2 mg dosing and predicted near-complete VEGF inhibition at q8/q12; no admissible DME patient test of the regimen exists.
dose.short: q12/q16 regimen predicted, no DME test
dose.quote: The model was then used to simulate 8-, 12- (quarterly), and 16-week dosing intervals in the clinic.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled full text). PALM (NCT02186119; abicipar 2 mg at weeks 0, 4, 8 then q12 or q8 vs ranibizumab; completed 2015-06) is the only DME trial of the regimen: no registry results, no peer-reviewed report found in Europe PMC. The q12 result in nAMD (CEDAR/SEQUOIA, Kunimoto 2020, doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2020.03.035) is outside this context. model_filed true: the EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (EMA/CHMP/279665/2020, section 3.2.2) describes 'an in silico mechanistic, multi-compartment PK model' built on ocular tissue data, with human abicipar and VEGF vitreal concentrations simulated over 52 weeks for the 2 mg phase 3 regimens, i.e. this model (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/withdrawal-report/withdrawal-assessment-report-rayoqta_en.pdf).
dose.reason: Regimen prediction never tested in DME
dose.judgement: The abicipar 2 mg q8/q12 regimens had already been dosed in DME (PALM, 2014-2015) and nAMD (CEDAR/SEQUOIA, 2015-2018) before the model was published, so any scoring would be a retrodiction under decision 10; but no DME patient result is admissible (no registry results, no paper, no regulator document for DME), so the cell stays untested with the model named. The EMA report adds that the model's 52-week simulations of 2Q8/2Q12 'resulted in permanent vitreal abicipar concentrations above the calculated IC50 value for VEGF inhibition' and 'support dose selection and treatment regimen of 2 mg/eye 2Q8/2Q12'; the regimen was nonetheless already in PALM and CEDAR/SEQUOIA before the model was public.

considered_not_added: DA VINCI phase 2 (Do 2011, doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2011.02.018, PMID 21546089, epub 2011-05-05; Do 2012, doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2012.02.010): not a model system; it is the earliest DME patient comparison for the existing diabetic-rat-brb-evans-blue and rabbit-ivt-pk-decay-model tracks and redates engagement 2, dose 2 and efficacy 2 to 2011 as the checker proposes; nothing to add under a new model_id.

Aqueous VEGF after intravitreal aflibercept in treatment-naive DME (doi 10.1089/jop.2020.0038, PMID 32589498; 16 patients, VEGF fell P<0.001 by month 2 after two monthly 2 mg injections): a direct-tier DME patient datum, not a model system; it belongs as a paired (comparison_stated false) engagement entry on the existing rabbit-ivt-pk-decay-model track (model_src Stewart 2008, PMID 18356264), which has no engagement entry in the draft; the rat track never measured VEGF. Not added here because the track exists.

Caruso 2020 cross-species ocular half-life scaling model (doi 10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.9b01191, PMID 31876425): aflibercept case study checked against pooled experimental human half-life (nAMD aqueous sampling), a retrodiction on literature data with no DME patient comparison; not added.

Regeneron 2026 integrated popPK of aflibercept 2 mg and 8 mg (doi 10.1002/psp4.70287, PMID 42381356; 14 weeks vs 9-9.5 weeks) and the PSP letter exchange 'Aflibercept 8 mg: from ocular clearance to pharmacodynamic duration' (reply PMID 42878418): the same popPK system as the BLA model, republished; no status change on aflibercept-hd-poppk-ocular, so no entry.

PALM (NCT02186119, abicipar 2 mg q8/q12 vs ranibizumab in DME, completed 2015-06): registry carries no results and no peer-reviewed report was found, so it cannot score the abicipar model's dose prediction; left as the untested note on that track.

Abicipar rabbit chronic retinal-neovascularisation leak model (Rodrigues 2018): already tracked as rabbit-chronic-rnv-leak; the Luu 2020 PK/PD model is a different system with a different prediction (human vitreal free VEGF), so it was given its own track rather than a post-hoc refit entry on the RNV track.

Rabbit ocular PK of conbercept after scatter laser (PMID 40260388, 2025) and monkey laser-CNV models of aflibercept/conbercept: no DME patient comparison (CNV models are nAMD); the STZ-rat conbercept work (Huang 2012) is already on the diabetic-rat-brb-evans-blue track.
Patient-derived organoids or cells, PDX, human challenge and human genetic models: none found for anti-VEGFA agents in DME in the searches above.
